correctness.rationale: Reconstructed ordinary UConf_2 of the specific 12-vertex Tietze graph via the Prue–Scrimshaw n=2 subdivision criterion (essential paths at least one edge; cycles at least 3). Explicit cubical chains have (66,180,117) cells; all signed ∂₁∂₂ compositions vanish. Independent modular rank of ∂₂ is 108; nine actual product two-cycles give a signed 9×9 unimodular coordinate minor −1, so ker ∂₂ is precisely Z⁹. All disjoint cycle pairs are exhaustively enumerated: 27 in six length families. Their length ≤10 subset has rank four, while nine integral basis tori have length ≤11. For the ten (3,6)+(5,6) tori, gcd of all ten maximal integer minors is 2 and each (3,5) torus has nonzero mod-two parity, establishing exact index-two obstruction and sharp cutoff. No assertion about arbitrary singular cycle length is made.

evidence: An–Knudsen establishes planar second-homology generation; Tietze has Petersen minor hence nonplanar. Prue–Scrimshaw supplies valid cubic model but no integral Tietze lattice. Farber papers and Barnett thesis treat ordered spaces and general families, not the asserted sharp cutoff.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A stronger all-graphs result giving H2 might entail some Betti numbers but not the extra specified simple-cycle length filtration and integral index. Nonplanar exceptional cycles make planar theorem inapplicable.
